title: Onramp weekly capture — quant & onboarding sprintlet
summary: Weekly standup capture from the onramp sprintlet focused on compact quant onboarding, quick eval checks, and triage for a problematic int4 rollout.
content:
Context: quick sprintlet (3 weeks) to accelerate onboarding of compact-precision variants for customer-facing models. Goal this week: stabilize the first int4 candidate, finish the small eval harness for prompt-set regression detection, and unblock infra for KV cache prefetch tests.

Attendees: Lin Zhao (owner), Marco Ruiz (bench), Aisha Patel (evals), Sofia Gomez (model-onboard), Tom B. (infra sync), Priya (SWE pairing) — plus ad-hoc: QA triage.

High-level notes / wins:
- Int4 candidate (cc-3b-compact-v1) now runs end-to-end on dedicated dev-GPU pool. Median latency p50 down ~28% vs fp16 on 2k context in our microbench harness.
- Added a lightweight eval runner that computes: prompt-pass-rate, hallucination-flag %, and edit-distance on structured-output tasks. Seeded with 120 diverse prompts from product-onboarding set.
- KV prefetch prototype integrated with local serving runtime (toy mode). Observed ~12% reduction in token compute for repeated prefixes in the microtrace.
- Onboarding checklist fleshed out: model card, quant config, kernel fallback policy, canary traffic plan, and a rollback playbook.

Quant experiments (replicable notes):
- Setup: dev-GPU A100-80GB, batch size 8, seq len 2048, 10 warmup sequences.
- Int8 baseline: quant-aware calibration w/ 2k calibration samples. Throughput: 310 toks/sec; p95 latency: 82ms.
- Int4 (symmetric per-channel) w/ second-order calibration: throughput: 410 toks/sec; p95: 99ms. Quality delta: avg prompt-pass-rate drop 3.4 percentage points, hallucination-flag +1.2pp (concentrated on numerical answers).
- Observations: int4 benefits throughput but shows brittle behavior on certain numeric and date-parsing prompts. Suspect range outliers in a small subset of MLP weights. Next step: targeted per-layer clipping + mixed-precision for final FF blocks.

Eval harness notes:
- Harness added for quick smoke and regression detection. Runs two modes: fast (120 prompts, ~4m) and deep (1.2k prompts, ~45m).
- Fast mode integrated into CI gating for model-onboard branch; configured to fail the PR on >5pp drop in prompt-pass-rate.
- Need: better metric for 'semantic drift' — current edit-distance noisy for long-form outputs. Aisha to prototype embedding-based similarity + thresholding by Friday.

Model onboarding checklist (status):
- model card: draft (Sofia) — needs token-cost estimate and quant profile.
- quant config: preliminary (Lin/Marco) — save config as v0.3 (attached in linked PR).
- kernel fallback tests: in-progress (Tom) — failing on 3/12 regression traces (OOM edge-cases).
- canary plan: design complete, waiting on infra quota (request submitted).
- rollout runbook + rollback: draft complete, will simulate in staging next week.

Blockers / open issues:
1) OOMs during fused-kernel path when batch size spikes — currently hitting in stress runs. Action: infra to add tighter cgroup limits and graceful fallback to non-fused kernels. Owner: Tom B. Target: 2026-09-17.
2) Numeric-answer drift in int4 on a subset of prompts. Action: run per-layer clipping experiments + compare symmetric vs asymmetric quant per layer. Owner: Marco. Target: 2026-09-20.
3) CI flakiness for deep-eval on PRs due to noisy network mounts. Action: move deep-eval to dedicated runner or cache datasets locally. Owner: Aisha. Target: 2026-09-22.

Action items (short list):
- Marco: run targeted per-layer clipping sweep (3 layer groups) and post results to JIRA-AM-8021 by 2026-09-20.
- Lin: finish canary traffic config + submit quota escalation ticket for dev pool by 2026-09-16.
- Aisha: prototype embedding-sim semantic drift metric and add to fast harness by 2026-09-17.
- Tom: patch runtime to avoid OOM on fused kernels (hotfix branch), add cgroup guardrails by 2026-09-17.
- Sofia: finalize model card with quant trade-offs and example failure modes by 2026-09-18.

Meeting adjourned notes / quick brainstorms:
- Idea: use a small calibration set that is dynamically sampled from recent production queries to reduce numeric outliers in quant ranges. Tradeoff: potential privacy/PII concerns — need legal/DSO check for sampling.
- Quick experiment: run int4 with mixed-precision only for FF blocks that show >2pp drop in per-prompt metrics. Could be a low-risk path to preserve most perf wins.

Appendix / links:
- quick bench script: github link in linked_artifacts PR (#197)
- draft model card: (internal confluence link) CONFLUENCE-ONRAMP-1423
- ticket for triage: JIRA-AM-8021

Notes-to-self: capture the targeted failure traces (ids listed in JIRA ticket) and include raw logits for the numeric prompts — will help postmortem for clipping approach.

Next sync: Monday 2026-09-20, 10:30am PT (15 mins). Focus: results from per-layer clipping sweep and infra OOM mitigation status.
